html:
The Nisqually are a Coast Salish people of southern Puget Sound, in today's Washington State, whose land runs along the Nisqually River from Mount Rainier down to the sea. They are part of the wider Coast Salish world and speak a dialect of Lushootseed.

Like their neighbours the Puyallup, they lived on salmon, shellfish, roots and berries, in villages of cedar plank houses. In 1833 the Hudson's Bay Company built Fort Nisqually on their land, the first European trading post on Puget Sound.

The Treaty of Medicine Creek of 1854 took most of their land and left them a small, poor reservation. The Nisqually leader Leschi refused it and fought in the Puget Sound War of 1855 to 1856. He was hanged in 1858; a historical court cleared his name in 2004. In the 1960s Nisqually fishermen such as Billy Frank Jr. led the "fish-ins" that won back their treaty fishing rights.
